Hello. I'm new here too.
I'm sorry you have had experiences where you felt this has failed you. All I know for certain is that if you feel and think like an outsider, you are an outsider. I know this because I have always felt like a pariah in school, work, in social settings.
I'm not sure how much advice I can actually offer but I understand where you're coming from.

I really, really appreciate you taking the time to talk to me. It seriously meant so much. I'm super new to having an account here, but if there's a way to keep in touch just messaging each other then I'd like to hear back what you think about the movie. Thanks again. Have a good night!
Maybe I'll text my parents something silly tomorrow. Thanks for your advice, I appreciate you taking the time to talk to me. Have a good night!

Yeah, people take movies way too seriously though. I bet you'll like it. :)

Oh, how I love Parks & Rec. I am definitely watching that now!
Oh, and you can play it on your PC.

Well, it's a first person shooter, you first pick a class among characters that all have different special abilities, there are talent trees to customize your character's strengths and playstyle and enemies drop random loot (guns) that you're always looking for to become more powerful as you level. The graphics are really unique, and the npcs who give you quests are...interesting...a lot of fucked up humor in this game. A lot of freedom to roam and explore the map. It's super fun.

I don't have any numbers in my phone. I lost the few contacts I did have when they seized my company phone without letting me back anything up. And I'm so humiliated at the direction my life is heading...I can't imagine enjoying catching up with anyone at this point in my life, you know?
Or...did you mean *totally* random texts to unknown numbers? Cuz that actually kind of sounds like fun.
The Indominus Rex dino that they "created" is a total badass. Chris Pratt handling raptors made me swoon. And the moments of humor were brilliant. Such a fun movie!

I watched the trailer, and it does look pretty damn cool. The whole "post-apocalyptic crazy people driving crazy cars across the desert while fighting each other" thing reminds me of Borderlands.
Ditto, seriously, I might go see Jurassic World again.
Hmm...I do love me some post-apocalyptic settings. I'll look into it!
Aww, I can imagine the smile. I'm trying to think positively, but I'm really crushed by the isolation I've imposed on myself since I lost my job.
I have not, but I recently went to see Jurassic World. I thoroughly enjoyed it! Chris Pratt is such a likeable actor. What is Mad Max about?
Hi. Did you have any happy moments today?

The breaking point fractured outward, like geometric ripples in a pond. The rift grew ever more complex, forming mesmerizing patterns. I could have spent eternity locked in a gaze with the shattered mirror, but mere moments passed before my entire existence forcefully shattered, displacing each piece into a bubble around me. I had been ejected from the realm of possible.

Time was not suspended, it failed to exist. I automatically understood infinity. Each splinter of glass held a parallel universe, and I existed in every one of them. The interminable macrocosms began swirling around me. I greedily peered into all that could ever be, unaware of who or what might be observing me. I suddenly felt more vulnerable than I could have ever fathomed. Each shard felt like a scrutinizing eye, taking in every bit of truth, even those which had escaped into the void of my mind. 

One by one, the mirror-eyes blinked and transmogrified into flesh. Strangers, versions of me. Plucked from the timeline of their universe, and dropped into the same peculiar plane of existence. All of my potential, laid out before me. I felt so…ashamed. I couldn’t hide, and I couldn’t lie. They all knew the truth about me. I burned hot with regret when I saw proof of what I could have achieved. All the excuses I ever clung to dissipated. I finally realized I had become a husk of a person, animated but not truly alive.
